newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent dips amid pre-expiry volatility.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent dips amid pre-expiry volatility.

text.p: IPE Brent was slightly lower on Tuesday in a fidgety market ahead of the May contract's expiry at the end of the session, traders said.
May Brent was 15 cents lower at $18.04 per barrel at 1015 GMT, while June was just five cents off at $18.29.
"There aren't any headlines out there," said one trader. "We've got the May expiry which everyone is impatient to get out of the way and then hopefully we'll see some type of break out."
Most traders expected June to hug a the $18 to $18.50 trading range for most the session, with the closure of the $18.65 to $18.77 gap remaining the next big challenge

One trader said a dip to $18.28 on the 60 minutes chart had sparked some temporary technical weakness in June but the contract had staved off the dwonward pressure pretty well despite some aggressive selling by one player.

Meanwhile, the Iran issue continued to lurk in the background, with news a senior Iranian government official had been linked to a group of Shiite Moslems suspected of bombing a U.S. compound in Saudi Arabia, seen as triggering much of Monday's gains.
"The whole Iran situation is still supportive," said one trader.
Gas oil was flat at $165.00 a tonne as it dabbled with resistance around the $165-$165.50 level.
Traders gas oil said it was drawing some support from stronger NYMEX heating oil.
